To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) for tasks that require associating words across long distance (e.g. semantic relation extraction, discourse parsing), recursive neural models are superior to sequential models; (2) sequential models can match the performance of recursive models if they are provided with a good sentence segmentation; and (3) the performance of both sequential and recursive models can be improved by using a larger vocabulary and by using more layers in the model.

(a) recurrent models are better at short distance tasks (b) recursive models are better at long distance tasks (c) recursive models are also better when the input sequence is long (d) recursive models can be replaced by recurrent models if the input sequence is broken into clause-like units.
